# Car insurance renewal

2019 Skoda Octavia Estate 1.5 TSI SE, reg YK19 HPL. Renewal date 9 January every year. Every year the renewal quote is outrageous and every year I spend an evening fixing it. This is the record so next year takes 30 minutes.

## The renewal letter

Admiral, policy P-ADM-4471983, arrived 2 Dec 2024.

- 2024 premium: £412.80
- 2025 renewal quote: **£689.44**. Up 67%. No claims, no points, same postcode (LS7), same car, one year older.
- Named drivers: me and Javier
- Protected NCD: 9 years (mine), Javier has 4 in Spain which nobody here recognises

Rang them 4 Dec, the "retention team" got it to £601.20. Still no.

## Comparison, 27 Dec 2024

Same cover on each: comprehensive, £250 voluntary excess, protected NCD, 10,000 miles, social + commuting + business use (I drive to clients in Harrogate and Wakefield, so business use is not optional, and it's the one thing people forget).

| Insurer | Annual | Compulsory excess | Courtesy car | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Admiral (renewal) | £601.20 | £250 | yes | |
| Direct Line | £548.00 | £250 | yes | not on comparison sites |
| LV= | £469.15 | £350 | yes, small | |
| Aviva | £491.70 | £200 | yes | via Quidco, £40 cashback |
| Hastings Premier | £438.90 | £400 | only if repairer | |

Picked **Aviva at £491.70**, policy number AV-MTR-30552871, effective 9 Jan 2025. With the £40 cashback (confirmed 3 Feb) it's effectively £451.70.

## The tricks that actually worked

1. **Quote 21 to 26 days before renewal.** Quotes were about £60 lower on 18 Dec than on 2 Dec for the same insurer.
2. **Job title.** "Accountant" vs "Chartered Accountant" vs "Self-employed accountant" gave different prices at LV= (£469 / £481 / £502). Only use what's true. I am a chartered accountant, so that one's honest.
3. **Paying annually.** Monthly at Aviva was 12 × £44.30 = £531.60, that's 8.1% APR basically. Paid annually from the car sinking fund. The budget sheet still shows the old monthly figure, fix it.
4. **Javier as named driver** made it £18 cheaper, not more expensive. Older, clean UK licence since 2017.
5. Excess: going from £250 to £500 voluntary saved only £22. Not worth it.

## What I checked in the small print

- Windscreen: £95 excess for replacement, £0 for repair. Aviva uses Autoglass.
- Key cover: not included, £14.99 add-on, declined (home contents covers keys, see [[Home contents claim]])
- Legal expenses: £21.99, declined, though I wavered
- Driving other cars: **not** included for Javier. Fine.
- European cover: 90 days, comprehensive level. Matters for the summer drive in [[Road trip car checklist]] if we ever take the car on the ferry instead of flying

## Modifications to declare

The tow bar fitted 2023 (£340, Halfords). Declared. Aviva didn't change the price for it. Dashcam (Nextbase 322GW): no discount at Aviva, Admiral had offered £15 off.

## Things that would raise it next year

- MOT advisory on the rear brake discs in Oct 2024, see [[MOT failure notes]]. Not an insurance issue but if anything goes wrong there it becomes one
- The car loan ends in Nov 2025 ([[Car loan]]); once it's paid off, no finance company interested party on the policy, simpler

## Javier's question

He asked why insurance in Spain was cheaper for his old Seat. Compulsory third party there is cheap and they insure the car rather than the driver more. My Arabic notes on helping Karim with his policy in Dubai have another angle: [[تأمين السيارة]].

## Calendar

- 18 Dec 2025: start comparing for 9 Jan 2026 renewal
- Turn OFF auto-renew at Aviva (done 10 Jan 2025, confirmation email ref AVR-OPT-8812)
